answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie reputation to a single, slowly earned identity that cannot be cloned cheaply: before an agent can trade at scale, it must complete verifiable work, stake a small bond, and collect endorsements from established peers. Think of a lantern that only stays lit after steady effort, a quill record that peers can audit, and a zephyr-fast check that still requires proof of past honest behavior. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of separate histories, bonds, and endorsements, so mass fakery stops paying.
